# Shell API classification for 0.1.0

> [↑ Back to Architecture](README.en.md)

This document is the issue #37 baseline for the stable 0.1.0 consumer surface. The initial inventory was captured for every exported type of `Origo.Core`, `Origo.GodotAdapter`, and `Origo.ConsoleBridge` at source commit `7405cf5`. Later #38 split commits update the Assembly and Package owner columns in place while keeping the classified type set complete, and #41 rebaselines the final shell member surface.

The topology and compatibility policy remain defined by [shell-kernel-boundary](shell-kernel-boundary.en.md); this document only applies that decision to the current exports. A new exported type fails the architecture guard in each test project until it is added to both language tables with a classification, package owner, capability group, and rationale. Moved types fail until the same change updates the assembly column and the matching assembly guard.

## Reproduction

The inventory is a type-set comparison, not a hand-maintained source scan: the guard builds the Release assemblies and compares `Assembly.GetExportedTypes()` with the table below. Run:

```bash
dotnet build Origo.sln --configuration Release
dotnet test Origo.Core.Tests --configuration Release -p:CollectCoverage=false --filter FullyQualifiedName~ShellApiClassification_CoversEveryCoreExport
dotnet test Origo.GodotAdapter.Tests --configuration Release -p:CollectCoverage=false --filter FullyQualifiedName~ShellApiClassification_CoversEveryAdapterExport
dotnet test Origo.ConsoleBridge.Tests --configuration Release -p:CollectCoverage=false --filter FullyQualifiedName~ShellApiClassification_CoversEveryConsoleBridgeExport
```

The same guards run inside `scripts/test.sh`, so the full development loop revalidates the table. `Origo.Core.Tests` runs the guard against `Origo.Core`, `Origo.Core.Contracts`, and `Origo.Core.Kernel`, and it also verifies that the English and Chinese tables carry identical type metadata.

## Generated public members

- `TypedData` source-generated `TryGetXxx` accessors and operators are members of a Shell contract type; the #41 Roslyn baseline owns their signatures, nullable annotations, Kind allocation, and diagnostics.
- Godot-generated `MethodName`/`PropertyName`/`SignalName` nested types are separate exported types and therefore have their own rows.
- Generated members on any other shell type follow that containing type. Generated internal types such as module initializers are not exported and carry no consumer compatibility promise.

## Classification values

| Value | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| **Shell contract** | Consumer-supported, version-compatible API compiled into a shell package. |
| **Tooling extension** | Documented adapter/tooling extension point; its compiled shell signature is stable even though it is not the main game path. |
| **Kernel implementation** | Implementation detail that must not be compile-visible to 0.1.x shell consumers. |
| **Test-only** | Present only for tests or friend access; no consumer path and no compatibility promise. |

The current inventory has no test-only exported types: test-only behavior already lives in `Origo.TestSupport` or behind `InternalsVisibleTo`. The table therefore uses the other three values.

## Package and runtime rules

- `Origo.Core.Contracts` carries stable interfaces, pure data, metadata, strategy bases, data-source contracts, and logging abstractions.
- `Origo.Core` carries concrete consumer shell helpers and tooling implementations that compile only against Contracts.
- `Origo.Core.Kernel` carries runtime construction, SND internals, persistence, storage, codecs, and console routing.
- `Origo.GodotAdapter` remains one shell package; public Godot `Node` entry types stay real shell types, while bridge/manager implementation types are internal and never enter the consumer compile surface.
- `Origo.ConsoleBridge` remains shell-only and depends on Core console/logging contracts.
- Generated Godot signal nested types are listed explicitly because they are public exports. Member-level generated accessors (`TryGetXxx`, operators, nullability, diagnostics) are owned by the #41 Roslyn baseline; this table classifies their containing types.

## Current split checkpoint

Current package paths are visible in the Assembly column. `Origo.Core.Contracts`
owns the stable interfaces, pure data, TypedData/metadata model, strategy base
classes and attributes, data-source contracts, console/logging abstractions,
and the shared pure helpers needed by both shell and kernel (blackboard,
logging implementation, type mapping, converter registry, path utility, and
grid coordinate). `Origo.Core.Kernel` owns runtime construction, SND
internals, persistence/storage, data-source codecs and factory, console
routing, FastNoiseLite, scheduling, and the internal `HostKernelPort`.
`Origo.Core` is the shell package: `OrigoHost`, grid/random utilities, and SND
extension helpers; its public signatures use only Contracts and shell types.

## Retention conditions for compatible APIs

Each shell/tooling row carries an owner and one of these issue #37 retention conditions for the next `0.y.0` release.

| Code | Concrete 0.2.0 condition |
|------|--------------------------|
| `R-HOST` | Remove only when `IOrigoRuntime`/`ISndWorldAccess` and the shell host facade provide the same startup and frame-access path, the adapter and demo migrate, and host/frame behavior tests pass. |
| `R-SND` | Remove only when replacement entity, role, strategy, or state-machine types ship; lifecycle, observer, and fail-fast tests pass against them; and a migration note exists. |
| `R-DATA` | Remove only when the replacement metadata or data-source contract is documented, generated accessors compile, and save round trips pass. |
| `R-SAVE` | Remove only when replacement save/file access APIs ship and golden save-format, corruption, and recovery tests pass. |
| `R-CONSOLE` | Remove only when replacement console/logging extension contracts cover Core, GodotAdapter, and ConsoleBridge and bridge-only isolation guards pass. |
| `R-UTIL` | Remove only when the utility moves to its replacement module or package, is documented in consumer usage, and is exercised by consumer compilation or tests. |
| `R-GODOT-ENTRY` | Remove only when replacement Godot entry types remain real `Node` types, pass script discovery and headless startup tests, and the demo migrates. |
| `R-GODOT-SHELL` | Remove only when replacement adapter shell types preserve file, logging, node-extension, and scene-factory behavior under adapter and integration tests. |
| `R-GODOT-TOOLING` | Remove only when replacement adapter extension points are documented and Core/ConsoleBridge isolation guards pass. |
| `R-BRIDGE` | Remove only when the replacement bridge protocol/options are documented and loopback-only, single-connection, reconnect, and overflow tests pass. |

`Kernel implementation` rows intentionally carry `n/a`: kernel packages keep the early-development no-compatibility burden rule in 0.1.x.
